# Resource Scheduler

> Free, MIT-licensed resource timeline for React: resources are rows and time runs across. Users drag to create, move and resize events, double bookings can be rejected, it works with keyboard and screen readers, and it is themed with CSS variables. Install from npm or copy the source into your repo with the shadcn CLI.

Facts to get the code right:

- npm package: `resource-scheduler`. Peer dependencies: React 18 or 19. Import the precompiled stylesheet once: `import "resource-scheduler/dist/resource-scheduler.css"`. No Tailwind setup is needed.
- shadcn alternative (copies the source, needs Tailwind v4): `npx shadcn@latest add mdobaid311/resource-scheduler/resource-scheduler`, then `import { ResourceScheduler } from "@/components/resource-scheduler"`. Skip the stylesheet import in that case.
- The component fills its parent, so the parent needs a height.
- It keeps no copy of your data. Pass `resources` (each with `id`, `name` and optionally `events`) and optionally a flat `events` list whose items name their resource with `resourceId` or `resourceIds`. Update your own state in `onEventCreate`, `onSlotSelect`, `onEventDrop` and `onEventResize`, then pass the new data back.
- An event is `{ id, title, startDate: Date, endDate: Date, color?, description? }`. `endDate` is exclusive: an all-day event ends at midnight of the next day.
- `ViewType` is a const object: `ViewType.Day`, `Week`, `Month`, `Quarter`, `Year`. Choose with `initialView` and `availableViews`.
- The day view is divided into slots: `slotDuration` (minutes), `dayStartHour`, `dayEndHour`. The other views use whole days. `weekStartsOn` (0 to 6) and `hideWeekends` apply to them.
- `onSlotSelect({ resourceId, start, end })` replaces the built-in event creation so you can open your own dialog. `onEventResize` turns the resize handles on.
- Conflicts: `eventOverlap={false}` forbids overlapping events on one resource, `isValidDrop(event, { resourceId, start, end })` is a final veto, `businessHours` and `Resource.unavailable` shade closed time and `blockUnavailable` rejects bookings there.
- `onRangeChange({ start, end, view })` fires on mount and when the visible range changes (`end` is exclusive): use it to fetch only what is on screen. A `ref` of type `ResourceSchedulerHandle` offers `goTo`, `setView`, `getVisibleRange` and `scrollToTime`.
- Recurring events: give an event `recurrence: { freq: "daily" | "weekly" | "monthly" | "yearly", interval?, byWeekday?, until?, count?, exceptions? }`. The scheduler draws one event per occurrence in the visible range; handlers receive an occurrence with `id` `"<id>::<yyyy-MM-dd>"` and `seriesId`, and you update your one series (add an exception for "this event only"). `expandRecurrence` and `expandEvents` do the same expansion outside the component.
- `findAvailableSlots(resource | resources, { from, to, duration, step?, businessHours?, limit? })` returns the free `{ start, end }` slots (for several resources, times when all are free). `virtualize` renders only the rows near the viewport; it is on by default above 100 resources and needs a fixed-height container.
- Languages: `locale` takes a date-fns locale (`import { de } from "date-fns/locale"`: names, date formats, 12/24-hour clock, first weekday), `hour12` forces 12 or 24-hour, and `labels` replaces any of the scheduler's text and screen reader messages (see `defaultLabels` for the keys). Leave `locale` out for the classic English output. `dir="rtl"` mirrors the layout for right-to-left languages (combine it with a locale such as `ar` and labels).
- Export: `eventsToICS(events, { resources?, name? })` returns an iCalendar string (timed events in UTC, whole local days as all-day events, `recurrence` as `RRULE`, `exceptions` as `EXDATE`, resource name as `LOCATION` when `resources` is passed) and `eventsToCSV(events, { resources? })` a CSV string (`id,title,resource,start,end,description`, one row per resource, formula-looking cells prefixed with a quote). Both take a flat event list (give each event its `resourceId`) and run in the browser or on a server. There is no import.
- Groups: give resources a `group` (a string) and they are listed under a collapsible header with that name, at the place the group's first member is; resources without one stay plain rows. `defaultCollapsedGroups`, or `collapsedGroups` with `onCollapsedGroupsChange` to control it. Headers are buttons (`aria-expanded`), the grid's arrow keys step over them, and events can be dragged between groups. A path nests a group: `group: ["Main building", "Floor 1"]` puts the floor inside the building, each level gets an indented header, and in `collapsedGroups` a nested group is its path joined with " / " (`"Main building / Floor 1"`); a one-name group keeps its plain name. `labels.group(name, count)` is the spoken text.
- Utilization: `showUtilization` draws a bar and a percentage under each resource name, the share of its available time that is booked in the visible range. Available time is business hours (the resource's own, else `businessHours`, else every hour) minus `Resource.unavailable`, times `Resource.capacity` (simultaneous bookings, default 1; it enforces nothing). Booked time is the part of the events inside the available time; overlapping events add up, so above 100% means overbooked. `getUtilization(resource, { start, end }, { businessHours })` returns `{ bookedMinutes, availableMinutes, ratio }` (`ratio` is `null` when nothing is available) for servers and reports; `labels.utilization(bookedHours, availableHours)` is its text.
- `classNames={{ root, toolbar, dateHeader, resourceCell, groupHeader, slot, event }}` adds classes to those parts, merged over the defaults with tailwind-merge (a conflicting utility replaces the default). With the npm package the utility must exist in your own CSS because the shipped stylesheet is precompiled; `event` is the default card, not a `renderTimeSlot` one.
- Colors come from `--rs-*` CSS variables, so a dark theme is a second set of values. Styles are scoped under `.rs-root` and do not leak.
- Next.js: the npm bundle starts with `"use client"`, so it can be imported from a server file.

Minimal example:

```tsx
import { ResourceScheduler, ViewType } from "resource-scheduler";
import "resource-scheduler/dist/resource-scheduler.css";

const resources = [
  {
    id: "ann",
    name: "Ann",
    events: [
      { id: "1", title: "Standup", startDate: new Date(2026, 9, 7, 9), endDate: new Date(2026, 9, 7, 10) },
    ],
  },
];

export function Board() {
  return (
    <div style={{ height: 480 }}>
      <ResourceScheduler resources={resources} initialView={ViewType.Week} eventOverlap={false} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Docs

- [Introduction](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/start/introduction/): what it is and is not
- [Installation](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/start/installation/): npm and shadcn
- [Quick start](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/start/quick-start/): a working board with create, move and resize
- [Data model](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/guides/data-model/): resources, events, flat events, end times
- [Views and slots](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/guides/views-and-slots/): views, slot length, week start, weekends
- [Load data and control the view](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/guides/loading-and-control/): onRangeChange and the ref
- [Creating events](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/guides/creating-events/): onSlotSelect and onEventCreate
- [Drag and resize](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/guides/drag-and-resize/)
- [Conflict control](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/guides/conflict-control/): eventOverlap and isValidDrop
- [Business hours and availability](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/guides/availability/)
- [Utilization](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/guides/utilization/): showUtilization, capacity, getUtilization
- [Resource groups](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/guides/resource-groups/): group, collapsedGroups
- [Export](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/guides/export/): eventsToICS, eventsToCSV
- [Keyboard and accessibility](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/guides/keyboard-and-accessibility/)
- [Theming](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/guides/theming/): the --rs-* tokens, dark mode
- [Next.js and SSR](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/guides/nextjs-and-ssr/)

## Recipes

Each has a live demo and the complete data model.

- [Room booking](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/recipes/room-booking/): no double booking, your own form
- [Shift roster](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/recipes/shift-roster/): recurring shifts, contracted hours, leave, utilization
- [Equipment rental](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/recipes/equipment-rental/): stock counts with `capacity` and `isValidDrop`, service days, finding free days
- [Field service dispatch](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/recipes/field-service-dispatch/): shifts, breaks, and booking the earliest technician with `findAvailableSlots`
- [Project allocation](https://resource-scheduler-demo.vercel.app/recipes/project-allocation/): whole-day allocations, project windows with `isValidDrop`, bench time with `showUtilization`
